# External coding agents (eca)

The two commands behind an eca agent (claude or codex run by aos, as in `templates/eca-claude`). People use `aos-agent` for both; run them by hand only to test.
turn:
# aos-eca-turn: one turn

```sh
AOS_STACK=/abs/st AOS_WS=/abs/ws aos-eca-turn /abs/def      # loop form; empty queue = exit 10
echo '{"prompt": "hello there"}' | AOS_STACK=/abs/st aos-eca-turn --one /abs/def
# FAKE: hello there        (tool form: prints the answer)
```

It is the body of an eca agent's loop. It hands every letter in `$AOS_STACK/queue` to the CLI as one prompt, waits for the answer and appends both to `history.jsonl`. DEF_DIR must be an absolute folder with `cli.json` (`AgentBad`); flags may go before or after it. `--on-empty idle` exits 0 on an empty queue. `--on-busy answer` waits instead of leaving the batch while someone is attached. A failure after the prompt was handed over (`CliFailed`, `ReplyMissing`) starts a cooldown (`cooldown.json`; `aos-agent ctl ls -l` shows it). A changed history starts a new conversation that carries the record over. A letter that is exactly `/clear`, `/compact`, `/status`, `/usage` or `/exit` (sent with `aos-agent say` or `chat`) is done by aos and answered with one `[aos] slash: ...` message (claude's own words for `/compact` and `/usage`): `/clear` moves `history.jsonl` to `history_removed.jsonl` and starts a new conversation; codex's `/compact` starts a new thread carrying aos's record; `/exit` closes the screen. After claude's `/compact` history is replaced by its summary. With the screen open, `/clear` and `/compact` are typed into it (not while it is answering). A letter starting with `/goal` (`/goal TEXT`, `/goal clear`, `/goal`) is the CLI's own goal, separate from aos's `goal.json`: typed into an open screen, otherwise handed to claude as it is (codex exec has no `/goal`; aos says so). When codex's screen then asks `Replace goal?`, aos picks `1. Replace current goal`; it presses nothing for a question it does not recognise. `TrustMissing`: see `aos/cli/errors.json#/codes`.
screen:
# aos-eca-screen: the screen

```sh
aos-eca-screen --eca /abs/def open --detach   # screen opened (...): /run/user/1000/aos-tty-1000/....sock
aos-eca-screen --eca /abs/def watch           # follows live.jsonl until one answer ends
aos-eca-screen --eca /abs/def close           # closed   (again: no screen (already closed))
```

People normally use `aos-agent open / close / watch -t NAME` (`aos/cli/talk_settings.json#/chat_screen`). It reads `AOS_STACK` (unset = `StackMissing`) and `AOS_WS`; ECA_DIR contains cli.json. `--eca` goes before the action; `--detach` goes after open and has no short name. open attaches unless detached; Ctrl-] (or Ctrl-\) leaves the screen running. close keeps the conversation and refuses while answering (`SessionBad`). watch ends after one answer, or when its daemon row stops running or disappears; if the daemon or table cannot be read, it keeps waiting. Ctrl-C leaves watch with exit 0.

Slash commands typed on the screen go to the CLI itself. aos follows it: when the CLI moves to another conversation (claude `/clear` or `/resume`), the next answer goes on in that one; `/clear` also empties the agent's `history.jsonl` (codex: when the answer comes from a thread that has only this turn; a thread with older turns is a `/resume` and history stays). claude's `/compact` keeps the conversation and replaces history with claude's summary (one `[aos] summary: ...` message); codex's `/compact` gives no summary text, so history becomes the user and assistant messages codex kept (read from its compacted `replacement_history`; tool definitions, tool calls and its own `<environment_context>` blocks are left out; if nothing can be read, history stays). The old messages move to `history_removed.jsonl`. `/exit` ends the screen; the next message is answered without one.
external_mcp:
# External MCP servers (claude and codex)

One server file per server; list them in `cli.json` as `"mcp_servers": ["mcp/site.json"]` (relative to cli.json, directives allowed). The CLI connects to them itself; a listed server is fully approved; `only` / `except` pick tools. Tool names are `mcp__<name>__<tool>`.

```json
{"description": "<one line>",
 "mcp_server": {"name": "site", "transport": "http", "url": "https://<host>:<port>/mcp",
                "bearer_token_env": "SITE_TOKEN", "env_file": "/home/<me>/.config/<agent>/site.env", "ca_file": "/home/<me>/.config/<agent>/ca-bundle.pem"}}
```

stdio: `"transport": "stdio", "command", "args", "env", "env_file"`; it is started through `aos-mcp-launch <server file>`, which reads env_file into the server process only.

- The token file is read when the CLI starts; codex gets the value only in its own environment and its shell does not (shell_environment_policy.exclude is added); claude gets it through headersHelper, never in its environment.
- `ca_file` sets SSL_CERT_FILE / CODEX_CA_CERTIFICATE (codex) or NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS (claude).
- A broken server file is skipped with a `cli_session: warning: external MCP server ... skipped` line; the others still attach.
- Never pass a secret with `aos-agent ctl add --envs`: it is stored in plain text in procs/<name>/exec.json.
- The other way: freeze the same server file into aos tools with aos-mcp-import (`aos/cli/mcp_import.json`); aos hooks then see the calls. Pick one way per server.
